_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Chromium version Orbit builds against.
Orbit embeds Chromium directly, built from real source -- no third-party
prebuilt. There are two ways to get a working build:
Scripts/chromium fetch              download Orbit's own published build
(fast; what CI and a normal clone use,
once the publish pipeline has run)
Scripts/chromium build --from-source gclient + gn + ninja a real Chromium
checkout under ThirdParty/chromium
(hours, tens of GB; opt-in)
The prebuilt that `fetch` downloads is produced by `build --from-source` on
a release machine and published as a GitHub Release asset -- see 'prebuilt'
below.
Each is built twice, in two configurations that differ only in gn's
dcheck_always_on: 'shipping' (false, what users get and what every
packaging path embeds) and 'dcheck' (true, what the Debug configuration
and the live-engine suites run against). Pass --config to any command.
To move to the newest Chromium: Scripts/chromium pin latest
To pin an exact version:        Scripts/chromium pin 151.0.7922.109
To see current state:           Scripts/chromium status
Nothing else in the codebase hardcodes a Chromium version. Every consumer
(xcconfig, Swift, Info.plist, user agent string) is generated from this file
by `Scripts/chromium sync`, which `pin`, `fetch` and `build` run automatically.

prebuilt._readme: Filled in per configuration by `Scripts/chromium record-prebuilt` after the release machine publishes a build for this pin. An empty platforms map means: fetch has nothing to download for that configuration yet -- run `Scripts/chromium build --from-source --config <name>` locally, or wait for the publish job.
